explanation: France has no cultural taboo around the left hand — that association comes from South Asian and Islamic hygiene customs, not French ones. In fact, Continental (French) dining etiquette keeps the fork in the left hand and the knife in the right for the whole meal, including bites, rather than switching the fork to the right hand after cutting as is common in the US.
local_tip: Keep your fork in your left hand and knife in your right throughout the meal — don't switch the fork to your right hand to take bites, as Americans often do.

also_check.note: The left hand is considered unclean and reserved for hygiene tasks; always eat and pass food with the right hand.
As in much of the Arab world, the left hand is seen as unclean; eating or handing food with it is frowned upon.
Chopstick etiquette is the main concern, not hand choice; left-handed use isn't stigmatized.
